title: The Roundabout
transcript: Fools will resign, but only a true genius would actually be able to find the incredible win that white has in this position. You see, white can get a new queen, but it is not that simple to make any progress because this is a completely open position and black can start to give checks to this white king. And if the king moves aimlessly, black always has a check and the move never passes to white. So, this would be a draw. But white realizes that he [music] can find shelter behind the opponent's king. So, he starts to go around via D4, C5, D6, E7, and finally goes to F7 and is now sheltered from the checks behind the black king. But there is a problem. Black has not run out of checks white yet because the black king can simply move out of the way and now open another check on the white king. Now, going back this way would allow black to repeat moves and there would be no progress to be made. And running this way would allow the F rook to keep giving checks and again draw the game. So, is this it? Is black simply out of the woods? Well, not exactly. White finds another [music] brilliant idea to make progress and starts to walk down with the king. And now, once this rook starts giving checks, we can realize that actually the rook cannot keep on checking this king or the king will march down towards the corner and eventually reach it. And this time, if black persists and gives one more check, we can sacrifice the queen for the two rooks and having one rook left, white would win the game. So, instead of keep checking with the same rook, black realizes that he has to use the E rook. Now, white only has one move, king to F3. And now, importantly, this forces black to keep checking with this rook rather than this one. And what difference does this make, you might think. We saw that black can just keep on checking the white king, but do you remember why we could not find shelter behind the black king? It's because from this position the king had a rook behind it and by moving he could still deliver a check. But now that we have switched the rooks the king does not have a rook behind him anymore. So, the solution is indeed to keep walking with the white king and go back around and behind the black king. And this time there is going to be no discovered check, which means that the solution to this puzzle is to take two full laps around the opponent's king, make the opponent run out of checks, and then convert to material advantage.
